title: Efficient R - How to write faster code

## Description

For most data analysis and statistical computing, R is efficient enough. However, there are times when we encounter bottlenecks in our code that slow it down significantly. In this lecture, I'll teach you techniques to identify those bottlenecks and write more efficient code. You'll learn the fundamental principles of faster R code and discover efficient packages for data analysis. We'll also touch on advanced optimization methods like parallelization and integrating C++ code. If you have previous experience with R programming and looking to make your R code run faster, this lecture is for you. If you are an R beginner, you'll still benefit from learning the principles and patterns and you will get a peak into some more advanced techniques.

## Links and resources

- For more details on good tool and project setup, an tips on writing good practice code, check out my talk ["Write R code that lasts: Practical tips for reproducible data analysis"](https://selinazitrone.github.io/tools_and_tips/sessions/10_r-code-that-lasts.html)
- [Book Efficient R programming](https://csgillespie.github.io/efficientR/) by Colin Gillespie and Robin Lovelace offers a great overview of different areas of efficiency
- [Youtube Video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EHoTFOW1WjU) on Writing efficient R code
- [Blogpost about profiling](https://support.posit.co/hc/en-us/articles/218221837-Profiling-R-code-with-the-RStudio-IDE)
- [Chapter in Hadley Wickham's Advanced R on performance](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/perf-improve.html)
- [Parllelization tutorials](https://henrikbengtsson.github.io/future-tutorial-user2022) for different use cases
- [Book chapter on Rcpp](https://csgillespie.github.io/efficientR/performance.html#rcpp)
- [Rcpp online documentation](https://www.rcpp.org/) with lots of info, tutorials and examples

### Mentioned R packages

- [profvis](https://profvis.r-lib.org/) for profiling R code
- [microbenchmark examples](https://www.statology.org/r-microbenchmark/) showing how to use the `microbenchmark` package to measure execution time of R code
- [data.table](https://rdatatable.gitlab.io/data.table/) for fast data import/export and manipulation
- [collapse](https://sebkrantz.github.io/collapse/) for fast data manipulation and analysis
- [arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/) for fast data import/export (especially for large datasets, even bigger than memory)
- [Rcpp](https://www.rcpp.org/) for integrating C++ code into R for performance-critical tasks
- [futureverse](https://www.futureverse.org/) overview of packages for parallelizing R code
    - [future](https://future.futureverse.org/) is the core package of the futureverse
    - [furrr](https://furrr.futureverse.org/) for parallelizing `purrr` functions
    - [future.apply](https://future.apply.futureverse.org/) for future apply functions
    - [dofuture](https://dofuture.futureverse.org/) for parallelizing for-loops and foreach-loops
